items.title: Reduction of the boundary-event estimate to a two-parameter Poisson integral bound
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia's coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:Bprob reduction 2` at source lines 1563-1569: for mu >= 1 and lambda in (0, 0.1 log x] the expectation of the indicator of |Z_i - u| <= mu/log x times the indicator of G(lambda) >= 4 times G(lambda)^2 is bounded by (lambda+mu) Delta. The author's proof (source lines 1571-1628) is a long chain in which every step is a different technique: a two-Poisson representation of the Dirichlet component with Gamma sums (lines 1572-1577), a combinatorial domination of the square of the counting variable by an ordered-pair sum (lines 1578-1586), an application of Mecke's equation turning that sum into a four-fold integral (lines 1587-1610), a change of variables that mixes the two Gamma variables into a single Beta variable t together with a comparison of dyadic ranges (lines 1611-1622), an explicit bound on the a-integrals using the log 5 estimate (line 1623), and finally the uniform Beta integral estimate that produces the factor (lambda+mu) (line 1627). The statement is a single inequality with no trace of this decomposition.
